# Translation bench: summary of the preserved runs

<!-- Generated by tools/translation-bench/summary.py from the runs in this directory. Do not edit by hand: `python3 -I summary.py` rewrites it, `python3 -I summary.py --check` fails when it is stale. -->

26 model runs on 5 models, one row per run. Every run is scored by `score.py` against the corpus snapshot it was preserved with (`runs/_corpus/<hash>`), over 312 planted probes in 14 sequences. Conditions: `A` today's request; `B2` + the previous 2 source lines; `W` + the window title, app and category; `M` + the user memory (window, document, people with speech levels, terms). A `(tg layout)` suffix is a bench prompt variant (README, Conditions); a `(t2 layout)` suffix is the product's own request (`RequestLayout`, README, The seam for T2): it sends the window card on every context request and no speaker channel, so its `B2` and `M` differ from the unsuffixed runs in more than the prompt text. Memory-only probes (`memory`) are the ones only the user memory can decide; `lines` need an earlier line; `none` are controls any engine should get right.

Reading the columns. **delta** is points of probe accuracy against condition A of the same model; **p** is the exact two-sided sign test on the probes where the two runs disagree (a default earns its place only against A with p < 0.05 on at least 250 probes). A run on another engine config of the same model (the `-fold` runs send the system prompt inside the user message) is compared with the A of that config. **Failed attempts** are replies that were not the JSON asked for or had the wrong number of lines, or timed out; the number in brackets counts those whose reply carried the context (it repeats a context line, or has more lines than items but no more than the context has lines). **Fallback lines** came from the stateless request after a failed attempt; **empty** lines no attempt translated (counted wrong). **Context leaks** are output lines that repeat a context line (the design's no-regression rule); **batch leaks** repeat another item of the same batch (condition A has these too: the model's own floor); **echoed** lines are their own source text returned untranslated. Latency is per request with retries included at `--jobs 1`; the machine was shared with other work, so latencies are comparable only inside one model's rows and carry the load shown. A latency verdict needs the A/A self-check of `latency.py` (the same condition A repeated; the preserved `A` and `A-r2` of gemma3:4b differ by 328 ms in the median).
